name: vLLM
description: A high-throughput and memory-efficient inference and serving engine for LLMs
editorialSummary: vLLM is the de facto open-source engine for high-throughput LLM serving. It pioneered PagedAttention and continuous batching, and remains the default choice for OpenAI-compatible GPU inference in production and research.
whyCare: If you need maximum tokens/sec on NVIDIA (and increasingly AMD/TPU) GPUs with an OpenAI-compatible API, vLLM is the starting point most teams standardize on.

name: llama.cpp
editorialSummary: llama.cpp is the foundational C/C++ runtime for running GGUF LLMs efficiently on CPU, Apple Silicon, and many GPUs. It powers a large share of local-AI tooling and defines the GGUF ecosystem used by Ollama, llamafile, and others.
whyCare: Best-in-class portable inference when you care about quantization, edge/CPU performance, and a dependency-light C++ core rather than a Python serving stack.

name: TensorRT-LLM
description: TensorRT LLM provides users with an easy-to-use Python API to define Large Language Models (LLMs) and supports state-of-the-art optimizations to perform inference efficiently on NVIDIA GPUs. TensorRT LLM also contains components to create Python and C++ runtimes that orchestrate the inference execution in a performant way.
editorialSummary: NVIDIA's optimized LLM inference stack compiles models into highly tuned TensorRT engines for maximum throughput and lowest latency on NVIDIA GPUs. It is the production path when you are all-in on NVIDIA hardware and need peak efficiency.
whyCare: Choose this when NVIDIA GPU utilization and latency matter more than cross-vendor portability—especially for large-scale enterprise serving.
notes: GitHub license metadata is NOASSERTION; treat SPDX as unverified.

name: SGLang
description: SGLang is a high-performance serving framework for large language models and multimodal models.
editorialSummary: SGLang is a high-performance serving framework focused on fast structured generation, RadixAttention for KV-cache reuse, and strong multimodal/MoE support. It competes directly with vLLM for cutting-edge throughput on modern GPUs.
whyCare: Strong alternative to vLLM when you need radix-cache efficiency, constrained/structured decoding, or leading multimodal and MoE serving performance.

name: Text Generation Inference
description: Large Language Model Text Generation Inference
editorialSummary: Hugging Face TGI was a major production LLM server used widely on the Hub and in enterprise deployments. The repository is now archived, but it shaped OpenAI-compatible serving patterns and remains historically important.
whyCare: Useful as historical reference and for understanding HF's serving stack; new greenfield projects should prefer actively maintained engines like vLLM or SGLang.
notes: Repository archived; prefer vLLM/SGLang for new deployments.

name: MLX
description: MLX: An array framework for Apple silicon
editorialSummary: MLX is Apple's array framework for machine learning on Apple Silicon, with unified memory and NumPy-like APIs. Together with mlx-lm it is the preferred path for efficient local LLM inference on Mac.
whyCare: If your target is Apple Silicon, MLX often beats generic CPU/Metal stacks for local model experimentation and fine-tuned inference workflows.
notes: Pair with ml-explore/mlx-lm for turnkey LLM loading and generation.

name: Sonar (Aphrodite Engine)
editorialSummary: Sonar is the continuation of Aphrodite Engine: a large-scale LLM inference server with broad accelerator support (CUDA, ROCm, TPU, Inferentia) and features like LoRA and speculative decoding. It targets community and production serving beyond a single-vendor stack.
whyCare: Consider when you want an Aphrodite-lineage serving engine with multi-backend hardware coverage and OpenAI-style APIs.
notes: GitHub redirects former Aphrodite-Engine/aphrodite-engine and PygmalionAI/aphrodite-engine here.

name: LMDeploy
description: LMDeploy is a toolkit for compressing, deploying, and serving LLMs.
editorialSummary: LMDeploy from InternLM provides Turbomind and PyTorch backends for compressing, deploying, and serving LLMs with strong performance on NVIDIA GPUs—especially popular in the Chinese open-source LLM ecosystem.
whyCare: Solid serving/compression toolkit if you deploy InternLM/Qwen-class models and want an alternative to vLLM with first-class Turbomind kernels.

name: MLC LLM
description: Universal LLM Deployment Engine with ML Compilation
editorialSummary: MLC LLM uses machine-learning compilation (Apache TVM) to deploy LLMs across phones, browsers, laptops, and GPUs from one stack. It emphasizes portable, compiled runtimes rather than Python-centric servers.
whyCare: Pick this when you need the same model runtime story across mobile, WebGPU, and desktop—not just datacenter GPUs.

name: CTranslate2
description: Fast inference engine for Transformer models
editorialSummary: CTranslate2 is a fast C++/CUDA inference engine for Transformer models with strong quantization support. It underpins many Whisper and translation deployments and remains a workhorse for efficient encoder-decoder and decoder-only inference.
whyCare: Excellent when you need a lean runtime for Whisper/translation/LLM-style Transformers with great CPU and GPU efficiency.

name: exo
editorialSummary: exo lets you run large models by partitioning inference across everyday devices on a local network—turning multiple Macs/PCs into a makeshift cluster for frontier-sized local AI.
whyCare: Interesting when a single machine cannot hold the model and you want distributed local inference without a datacenter rack.

name: BitNet
editorialSummary: Microsoft BitNet is the official inference framework for 1-bit (and low-bit) LLMs, focusing on extreme quantization for efficient CPU inference. It represents a distinct efficiency path versus standard GGUF INT4/INT8 stacks.
whyCare: Watch this if you care about ultralow-bit local LLMs and CPU-first efficiency research moving into usable runtimes.

name: LoRAX
description: Multi-LoRA inference server that scales to 1000s of fine-tuned LLMs
editorialSummary: LoRAX is a multi-LoRA inference server designed to host thousands of fine-tuned adapters on shared base models. It targets production multi-tenant serving where each customer or task has its own LoRA.
whyCare: Use when adapter density matters—serving many fine-tunes efficiently without loading a full model copy per adapter.
